steps.what: Confer with producers and performers to determine and achieve the desired production sound

tasks.design: Keep creative sound discussions with the technician, producer and performers. Reference material in {DOCS} can support listening and discussion without replacing agreement on the sound.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creative intent is contextual and often expressed through listening and comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reference playback and shared documents remain available.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling different preferences and translating them into an achievable sound.
tasks.human_edge: Listening, interpreting intent and negotiating a common direction.
tasks.altitude: Creative responsibility and working time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Agreeing a desired sound requires contextual listening and collaboration; no task-specific labour reduction is established.

assumptions: Boundary covers creative discussion and agreement, excluding equipment setup and mixing execution.
Participants provide preferences through existing discussion; technician interpretation is counted in s1. No structured sound-style code or automatic preference extraction is assumed.
Consider native reference-sharing features before custom code; no new system is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the collaboration method remains unchanged.
unknowns: Production types and current revision patterns
research_questions: Is repeated documentation a measurable part of creative discussions?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Listening and creative agreement retain full time; no clerical baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Separate and combine sounds in the mix

steps.what: Separate instruments and vocals, combine sounds and refine the mix by listening

tasks.design: Retain separation, balance and mix decisions in the audio workstation {OTHER}. Existing processing tools are already part of the technician's baseline; no specific new removal of listening or adjustment time is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mix quality depends on taste, source recordings and production intent.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing audio processing supports the current workflow.
tasks.still_hard: Artefacts, masking, balance and whether the result serves the performance.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing problems and choosing the intended musical or dramatic effect.
tasks.altitude: Mixing responsibility and working time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Align sound choices with picture intent

evidence.claim: Sound mixing requires creative listening and judgement; existing audio processing runtime does not establish a new labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is sound separation and mixing, excluding recording setup, creative direction meetings and final distribution.

The {OTHER} slot is the audio workstation. Technician inspects supplied tracks and their identity within s1; no clean stems, structured instrument labels or quality flags are assumed without checking.
Test existing workstation processing features before custom code; no new separation model or automatic mix release is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the current mixing method and tools remain unchanged.
unknowns: Recording quality and existing separation tools
Time spent on repetitive technical processing versus creative adjustment
research_questions: Can session logs isolate repeat technical operations that are not already automated?

tasks.short: Report equipment faults and ensure repairs

steps.what: Report equipment problems with symptoms and affected equipment identity
Ensure required repairs are completed and check equipment suitability before reuse

tasks.design: Retain fault reporting through {EMAIL} or {TELEPHONY} and practical repair follow-up. A reminder system might help repeated chasing, but that workload has not been established in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Symptoms and repair adequacy require direct equipment knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication channels support fault reports.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults and verifying that repaired equipment performs correctly.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a problem that a repair completion message does not resolve.
tasks.altitude: Repair coordination responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Signal path testing and repair handoff requirements

evidence.claim: Reporting faults and verifying repair suitability require contextual technical judgement; no task-specific saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is fault reporting and ensuring repair completion, excluding the repair technician's physical repair labour.
Technician identifies the equipment and symptoms in s1. Repair personnel produce their response after receiving the report and before s2; no ready-made completion or safe-to-use flag is assumed.
Consider native fault tracking before custom code; no new reporting requirements are imposed on repair staff.
Zero incremental upkeep because reporting and practical verification remain unchanged.
research_questions: Does repeated status chasing consume measurable time separate from technical verification?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Fault reporting and repair verification retain full time; supplier repair labour is outside the denominator.

tasks.short: Select and set up recording microphones

steps.what: Prepare recording sessions by selecting, positioning and testing microphones and signal paths

tasks.design: Keep microphone selection, physical setup and listening tests with the technician. Existing session notes in {DOCS} can guide preparation but do not establish correct placement or signal quality.
tasks.previous_blocker: Microphone performance depends on the performer, room and intended sound.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing equipment and session notes remain available.
tasks.still_hard: Placement, acoustic interactions and avoiding recording faults.
tasks.human_edge: Listening to the actual setup and adapting it before recording.
tasks.altitude: Setup responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Local routing and equipment testing practices

evidence.claim: Microphone preparation includes physical placement and listening checks; no software labour saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is recording setup and checks, excluding creative brief agreement and later mixing.
Technician assesses room, performer, microphone choice, routing and signal quality within s1; no structured acoustic model or setup-ready flag is assumed.
Consider native equipment presets before custom code; no new system is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because equipment preparation remains unchanged.
unknowns: Session types and reusable setup patterns
research_questions: Is any repeated clerical setup separate from physical placement and listening checks?
